measured.limits: Small synthetic local samples; not a network/cloud/real-device benchmark. Seed construction uses fixed real models/INSERT/scope records, not repeated Admin HTTP; it is performance setup, not lifecycle correctness evidence. Global dependency drift from baseline is not isolated. No resource or formal-release gate is closed.
measured.method: Same installed dependencies, exact baseline repo/endpoint function source compiled in isolated namespaces; shared current model/schema/guard dependencies. Old scope function uses current immutable scope types. Five alternating fresh DB-copy HTTP requests per side/size, real auth/Pydantic/SQLite write, no lifespan or sockets. Each independent size group resets only its local synthetic limiter fixture; ten requests remain under the unchanged actual 30-request limit. SQL timings warm cache and alternate order. Empty HTTP history baseline initializes an extra default row, so its business semantics differ and it is not a like-for-like latency comparison. The separately timed legacy get_policy path uses independent default-root histories with scheduled future versions, checks complete Policy rows unchanged on nonempty reads, and compares full selected effective Policy values; empty legacy calls intentionally bootstrap one default on both sides.

caveats: HTTP tests are TestClient ASGI calls, not TCP/TLS or deployed service latency.
The baseline executes exact9654 repository source and exact endpoint function AST, with shared installed dependencies/model/schema/security helpers.
Fixture direct fixed model/INSERT/scope setup is performance preparation, not lifecycle or authorization-correctness proof.

Raw reserved roots/forks and foreign/unregistered children are deliberate synthetic query-equivalence faults; ambiguous tips remain visible for caller rejection, not a claim of arbitrary raw-SQL defense.
Five samples and a single Windows host give directional observations; build/other host workload and filesystem caches are not globally isolated.
preOptimization.harnessDifferences: This earlier qualified stage did not yet add the separately timed legacy reads or full successful-response equality assertions. Actual timed append call, fresh-copy method and exact baseline source loading were unchanged.

conclusions: No greater-than20percent median regression was measured for successful like-for-like Admin append or nonempty legacy reads. At1000versions actual Admin HTTP median fell from1907.6823ms to1097.6182ms; nonempty legacy effective read was1075.1785ms to1080.1359ms.

Empty legacy bootstrap rose from16.9263ms to19.0597ms, about12.60percent/WARN and2.1334ms absolute. It now observes an empty tip before initialization; this warning is retained without raising thresholds.
Empty Admin POST does different intended work: baseline persists hidden default plus explicit root, current persists only explicit Admin root. Its relative latency is NOT_COMPARABLE.
The original production Policy view traverses a recursive chain and remains the dominant1000-version cost; no view, index, schema, scope or final write-CAS guard was changed for speed.

Successful nonempty append response models matched completely on all15pairs. All20legacy effective Policy selections matched, and nonempty Policy rows were unchanged. SQL candidates retained identical result sets in8scope/NULL/fork/fault cases.
causesAndSmallestFixes: Correlated child anti-join repeated work during tip observation and final append checks; root changed only this fixed query to an explicitly NULL-filtered NOT IN form.
Recursive production-view traversal remains expensive at1000versions. A future indexing/view change needs explicit schema/migration and isolation review; it is not authorized or included here.
Local transaction/auth/model cost dominates short histories. Avoid optimizing away empty-chain observation, permissions, history or finalCAS to remove the small initialization WARN.
